approved: Education Services for Overseas Students Amendment Bill 2013
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would clarify how education providers handle pre-paid fees from overseas students.
It would give the Minister power to set refund calculation methods by legislative instrument when a student's visa is refused or no written agreement exists.
The bill would also update the title of the National Code to remove reference to registration authorities, which no longer apply after 2012 amendments.
Clarifies existing provisions on pre-paid fees under the ESOS Act.
Gives the Minister power to make a legislative instrument for refund calculations in cases of visa refusal or missing written agreement.
Amends the title of the National Code to reflect it now applies only to registered providers.
Overseas students and registered education providers under the ESOS Act.

Supported the Education Services for Overseas Students Amendment Bill 2013, reporting that nine providers closed in 2012-13, affecting 907 students, and warned that the Tuition Protection Service fears up to 22 more providers with around 4,400 students could close in the coming financial year.

Supported amendments strengthening the Tuition Protection Service to guarantee refunds for international students when providers fail or visas are refused, noting international education is a $15 billion export supporting 100,000 jobs, and cited a report predicting up to 22 providers serving 4,400 students would close through default.

Supported technical refund amendments to the overseas students bill, noting Australia's education exports grew from just over $2 billion in 1996 to close to $19 billion by 2009 before declining 20 to 25 per cent under Labor, and criticised the national curriculum's sustainability priority as an ideological 'green doctrine' at odds with economic progress.

Supported strengthening the Tuition Protection Service, recalling that 49 higher education providers closed in 2009 and 2010 alone, displacing more than 11,000 students, noted the scheme collected $6 million in levies in 2013-14, and criticised the coalition's $2.3 billion cut to education funding.
